failure_summary.description: Calls misbound fields or values, misplaced parameters, or omitted requested optional constraints and selectors.
Some calls used endpoints or batching that did not match the distinct requested result or the benchmark's endpoint mapping.
An opaque numeric lookup ID was guessed from a location name rather than resolved or left unset.

patch.reasoning: Most batch failures are already addressed by the skill's endpoint-matching, parameter-placement, and canonical-value rules, so repeating those instructions would add little. Add a narrow guard for opaque lookup IDs, which the current guidance does not explicitly distinguish from values that can be derived from a name.

edits.target: - When a schema splits one supplied identifier across component fields, parse it according to those field definitions and pass each component only to its corresponding field (for example, a username/local part and a domain). Do not repeat the entire compound identifier in each component field.
edits.content: - Do not guess opaque lookup identifiers (such as numeric country or catalog IDs) from a name. Use a documented lookup or an explicitly supplied/canonical value; if no mapping is available, leave an optional ID filter unset and use any supported textual filter instead.
